thread:
IncidentBot: detected high error rate (502/504) from inference fleet in eu-west-1a, alert severity: P1. source: ALB healthcheck anomalies + instance network metrics spike. https://status.aws.amazon.com/somepage :rotating_light:
PagerDuty: Paging Sophia (oncall).
Sophia: acked. looking. can someone confirm customer impact (latency/errors) windows?
Matt: seeing 30% of requests for model-prod-3 failing with 504s, tail latency spiking to 8s. dashboards: /d/redwood/inference/latency (internal).
Olivia: oncall-runbook link: https://runbook/internal/az-network-degen. first step: check ENI / instance network counters and node reprovisioning events.
Ryan: pulling instance metrics now. ena_rx_drops and netpackets_dropped on g5.xlarge in eu-west-1a. a couple of instances show RX queue saturation.
Sophia: good. set routing policy to avoid eu-west-1a for model-prod-3 if possible. can we steer to eu-west-1b and fallback region eu-central-1?
Matt: routing policy change in router-config enacted: add region preference to avoid zone eu-west-1a for model-prod-3. command run:
```
# set routing policy
redwoodctl route update --model model-prod-3 --avoid-az eu-west-1a --max-penalty 0.8
```
Matt: also increased cross-region burst capacity to allow temporary overflow: `redwoodctl capacity bump --region eu-central-1 --pool inference-burst --duration 30m`
IncidentBot: automated check: route change applied, traffic shifted ~55% off eu-west-1a within 90s.
Olivia: DNS note: some clients have cached endpoints to eu-west-1a. TTL is 60s but some networks have longer caches. consider lowering TTL for control-plane endpoints and push new mapping.
Sophia: lowering public API-TTL might be disruptive. instead, we'll add an explicit ALB-level redirect: mark eu-west-1a target-group unhealthy for model-prod-3 until network is stable. doing that now.
Ryan: marking tg-az1a-model-prod-3 unhealthy -> traffic drops to 12% within 2 minutes. error rate falls but still seeing intermittent 502s from a subset of nodes.
Matt: spinning up replacement Dedicated nodes in eu-west-1b and warming models. `redwoodctl node create --region eu-west-1b --type g5.4xlarge --count 4 --labels warm`
CustomerSuccess: heads-up: CS team reported 3 enterprise customers saw transient 504s between 06:12-06:20 UTC. they want ETA and whether any data lost.
Sophia: ETA: traffic mostly stable, but we'll keep mitigation active for next 30m. no known data loss - inference requests are stateless; retries handled by client. I'll post a brief status update to #general and to customer status page.
Sophia: posting status: "We are investigating elevated errors for eu-west-1a impacting some inference requests. Traffic is being rerouted; we expect reduced errors within 10-20 minutes. No data loss. More updates in this thread." :information_source:
Matt: logs show intermittent TCP resets on instances provisioned in the same AZ host pool. suspect host-level network driver/kernel flaps. opened AWS support case 1234567890.
Olivia: AWS case acked, they see "hardware network card resets" on a subset of hosts. recommending instance replacement by AZ. estimating remediation time 45-90 minutes if they replace hosts.
Ryan: continuing to replace nodes on our side. draining unhealthy nodes: `kubectl drain node/node-xyz --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then cordon and terminate.
IncidentBot: automation: draining sequence started for 8 nodes in eu-west-1a. progress: 3/8 drained.
Sophia: switching primary oncall to Matt for the next 30m, I'm handing off. Matt, take it.
Matt: taking it. I'm watching the routing mitigation and AWS case. next steps: let replacements warm, keep tg-az1a unhealthy until 95% of replacements healthy. also prepare rollback plan in case cross-region capacity saturates.
CustomerSuccess: flagged two customers for immediate SRE DM with post-incident summary.
Matt: created incident ticket INC-2026-042 with timeline. adding follow-up owners: @Olivia (infra), @Ryan (node repair), @Sophia (postmortem).
Olivia: note for postmortem: gather kernel logs, ENA/driver versions, AWS host IDs, and ALB target health transitions. also collect fallback latency delta (eu-west-1b vs eu-west-1a).
Ryan: replacements up: 6/8 nodes replaced and healthy, model warmers complete on new nodes. request success rate back to 99.6% across region.
IncidentBot: automated verification: error rate back to baseline. continuing monitor for 20m.
Matt: setting reminder: re-enable tg-az1a when nodes fully healthy and AWS confirms root cause resolved. current plan: leave unhealthy and monitor for 1h after baseline.
Sophia: oncall handback: I'll take morning follow-up and run the postmortem. please record any customer-impact notes in INC-2026-042.
CustomerSuccess: thanks team — CS will notify impacted customers with the summary and offer a follow-up call if needed. :pray:
Matt: closing active P1 mitigation. moving thread to "monitoring" and will update incident status page once AWS confirms host replacements finished.
IncidentBot: incident state -> mitigated. metrics will continue to be collected.
Sophia: postmortem owner assigned. action items: (1) add quicker AWs host replacement runbook step; (2) investigate proactive host health sampling in eu-west-1a; (3) revisit routing policy thresholds.
Matt: thumbs up. I'll update runbook and add a small automaton to mark target-group unhealthy when tcp reset rate > X over 30s.
IncidentBot: thread closed for now. follow-up notes will be appended to INC-2026-042.
